    SAUC and its confidence interval

    sauc.Rd

    This function calculates the area under the SROC curve (SAUC) of the bivariate random-effects model, and its confidence interval when the variance-covariance matrix of the estimates is given.

    sauc(mu1, mu2, tau1, tau2, rho, var.matrix = NULL, ci.level)

    Arguments

    mu1

    The mean of the logit-transformed sensitivity.

    mu2

    The mean of the logit-transformed specificity.

    tau1

    The between-study standard deviation of the logit-transformed sensitivity.

    tau2

    The between-study standard deviation of the logit-transformed specificity.

    rho

    The between-study correlation of the logit-transformed sensitivity and specificity.

    var.matrix

    The 5 x 5 variance-covariance matrix of the estimates of (mu1, mu2, tau1, tau2, rho) in this order, such as var.ml in the output of reitsma.sroc. If var.matrix = NULL (default), the confidence interval is not calculated.

    ci.level

    The confidence level of the confidence interval, within (0, 1). It is required when var.matrix is given.

    Value

    A named numeric vector of sauc, sauc.lb, and sauc.ub (SAUC and the lower and upper bounds of its confidence interval). sauc.lb and sauc.ub are NA if var.matrix = NULL, and sauc is NA if the integration failed.

    Details

    SROC curve

    The SROC curve is \(\mathrm{Se} = \mathrm{logit}^{-1}(\mu_1 - (\rho \tau_1 / \tau_2) (\mathrm{logit}(x) + \mu_2))\), where \(x\) is the false positive rate (1 - specificity). SAUC is its integral over \(x \in (0, 1)\) by integrate.

    Confidence interval

    The standard error of SAUC is calculated by the delta method. The confidence interval is calculated on the logit scale and back-transformed, so it is not symmetric around SAUC.

    See also

    reitsma.sroc, srocsa.t

    Examples

    ## SAUC without confidence interval
sauc(mu1 = 1.5, mu2 = 2, tau1 = 0.8, tau2 = 0.9, rho = -0.3)
#>      sauc   sauc.lb   sauc.ub 
#> 0.8752776        NA        NA 

## SAUC with confidence interval from the fitted model
data(IVD)
fit <- reitsma.sroc(TP = TP, FN = FN, FP = FP, TN = TN, data = IVD)
est <- fit$par
sauc(mu1 = est[1], mu2 = est[2], tau1 = est[3], tau2 = est[4], rho = est[5],
     var.matrix = fit$var.ml, ci.level = 0.95)
#>      sauc   sauc.lb   sauc.ub 
#> 0.8735863 0.8057723 0.9200719
